items.evidence: python roll.py --headless --ticks N --inputs/--script --board B --settings DIR printed one JSON object with tick, screen, board, score, lives, ball, coins, crates, bridge_x, volume, language, selected, texts, sounds (e.g. --ticks 5 --inputs 1:enter -> screen play, board 1).
--frame wrote PNGs for title, settings, play boards 2 and 3, paused, won, lost; all have a valid PNG signature and IHDR 800 x 480.
python roll.py --all-wavs DIR (and the ready files in sounds/): coin 0.30 s, bounce 0.15 s, fall 0.90 s, clear 0.80 s; each peak 29490; zero crossings/s 2457, 127, 660, 1595; all four hashes differ.
tick 1: title, selected Start. menu_down -> Settings, again -> Quit, again -> Start (wraps); menu_up from Start -> Quit. 1:enter -> screen play, board 1, score 0, lives 3, ball at (0, 1.2255, 0).

Settings opens with texts Volume: 8, Language: English. Four menu_right -> 10 (capped); two menu_left -> 6; 14 menu_left -> 0 (floored); menu_right on Language -> es, again -> en; enter on Back -> title.

With es saved: title [Roll, Empezar, Ajustes, Salir]; settings [Ajustes, Volumen: 6, Idioma: Espanol, Atras]; play [Tablero 2 de 3, Puntos: 0, Vidas: 3]; paused adds Pausa, Continuar, Volver al titulo; won [Has ganado, Puntos: 30, Pulsa Intro...]; lost [Fin de la partida, ...]. No English left.
Run 1 with --settings judge-scratch/set1 set volume 6 and es (settings.json written); run 2 with the same folder started at 6, es (title and play). A run without --settings started at 8, en.
--board 1, no input: y first <= 0.3 at tick 27; rises again (max 0.505) after landing; at tick 600 y = 0.2488; sounds = 3 x bounce.
Push held ticks 60-90 then none: right -> x 0.51 at 90, 1.48 at 120, 2.38 at 150; left -> -x; up -> -z; down -> +z (same magnitudes). The ball keeps moving for 60 ticks after the push ended.

Generated script cleared board 1 (CLI --board 1, 505 vs 506 ticks): score 30 -> 40, last coin gone, sounds end coin, clear; board 2, ball (-3, 1.25, 0) at rest, board 2's three coins and six crates in state. Each earlier coin also added exactly 10.
--board 2, no input, 300 ticks: six crates at (0, 0.25/0.75, -0.5/0/0.5); max deviation from their places over all 300 ticks 0.0.

--board 2 0:right: ball reaches x >= 1 at tick 99 (on board 1 with the same push it covers 4 m by about tick 85); at tick 300 four crates are 0.5-1.06 from their places and one was pushed off; no crate ever had y < 0.2 while over the board.
Same run: a crate pushed off at x ~4.2 falls (y -4.93 at tick 208) and the crates count goes 6 -> 5 at tick 209; the other five remain.

Board 1 script with a fall first: tick 136 lives 3 -> 2, fall in sounds, ball (0, 1.25, 0), coin taken stays taken; board 2 began with lives 2 and a fall there made it 1, ball back at (-3,1.25,0), crates where they were, coins unchanged.

Ball resting on the bridge from tick 420: ball.x - bridge_x stayed -0.83..-0.84 through 800 (bridge went 0.67 -> 2 -> 0 -> 0.67), y 0.2495, no fall. Pushed right at tick 100 while bridge near 1.9: ball dropped into the gap, life lost at ~tick 240.
Generated script (judge-scratch/b3script.txt) with --board 3: won at tick 607, score 30, texts You win / Score: 30; ticks to 900 with left/none pushes changed nothing; 910:enter -> title.
--board 2 0:right: lost at tick 588, lives 0, score 10; at tick 800 after left/up/down pushes the state is identical (score 10, ball/coins/crates null on this screen, sounds same); enter -> title.

--board 2 150:escape: state at 151 and 400 identical (ball, crates, score); --board 3 100:escape: ball and bridge_x 1.1111 identical at 101 and 300; enter on Resume -> play and ball moves on; menu_down + enter (Quit to title) -> title.
Two board 2 runs (strike plus pushes, 400 ticks) printed byte-identical JSON (same md5), crates after the strike included; two board 3 runs of 700 ticks also identical.

b2strike.png: board 2 seen from above and in front in perspective, whole slab visible, shaded blue sphere with highlight at the right edge where x=4.07, crates as brown boxes with shaded faces in the wall and one off the edge, two remaining coins. b3.png at bridge_x 0.44: two slabs, gap, bridge drawn a little right of the gap's left edge.

Title, settings, paused, won frames show their Spanish texts and the play frame shows TABLERO 2 DE 3, PUNTOS, VIDAS; but the Spanish lost frame (es_lost.png) cuts the banner to N DE LA PARTI: Fin de la partida runs off both sides of the 800 px frame.

gui.py:66 plays only when volume > 0 and uses sound.wav_bytes(name, volume), where sound.py:53 scales gain by volume/10; --wav NAME --volume 0 wrote all-zero samples; sounds list still recorded in state.
README has Play controls, exact commands for the headless run, the frame (--frame) and WAVs (--wav / --all-wavs), all ran as written, and a Files section saying which file holds what.

defects: Spanish Game over banner (Fin de la partida) is drawn wider than the 800 px frame and is clipped on both sides.
Coins are drawn as upright discs at a spinning angle, so one can show as a barely visible thin sliver in a frame (coin at (-1.5, 1.5) on board 2).
On lost/won screens the state nulls ball, coins and crates, so the frozen board cannot be confirmed from the state alone (the code does stop stepping).

where.how: weighted_by_kind is exact (the run's own token counts times the weights); a step's kind is a reading of its command's text, and answered_tokens / written_tokens are characters / 4

trace.how: context, new, read_again and how far the context grew are the run's own records. written_out a request is its growth less its answers (characters / 4), scaled to the run's exact total; of_which_unseen is that less the visible text (thinking). cost is what the request read and wrote, weighted; carried is what reading again what it added cost at every later request (start.carried: the same for what every request starts from). reading + writing is in_the_ledger
